original_title: [Medium][NATIVE-005] WebView request state is not reset consistently on Desktop, iOS and Web
classification: Medium, confirmed-source owning Reload defect; added genuine runtime fixtures remain uncompiled/unexecuted

source_locations.root_cause: After unsupported URL B rejection or HTTP redirect, state.requestedUrl can differ from readable native current A; old Reload beganRequest(B) while location.reload() loads A.

original_criteria.text: - Fail→success, fail→fail, reload, stop and redirects on every target.

Separately complete actual Android/Desktop/iOS failure/reload/stop/redirect matrices; accepted common/identity cases are not substitutions.

browser_semantics: Opaque sandbox srcdoc does not expose parent DOM/storage even with allow-scripts; allow-same-origin is still absent. Sandbox changes govern later navigation, not immediate revocation of a committed Trusted document.

Trusted test content is host-controlled only; same-origin readable window.location/stop can be observed. Opaque/cross-origin window.stop/history/evaluation remain browser-protected; no unsafe workaround or fabricated completion is introduced.

Framing/network failure may fire load rather than error, with inaccessible error-page metadata. A terminal event is not HTTP/CSP/TLS/authentication success. New refusal witnesses additionally require actual owned request/close receipts and old-document clearance.
No popups/user-gesture/nested/CSP/security replay is needed for closed #11. Its accepted automation-popup assumptions are retained, not promoted to physical activation or other-engine proof.
PostMessage sender wildcard is restricted by receiving exact native iframe WindowProxy identity, same origin, trusted event and session token; no library bridge or CORS bypass is claimed.

compatibility.intentional_correction: Readable native Reload records the actual reloaded current URL, not a previous rejected or redirect-start URL; opaque/cross-origin fallback still uses last accepted content.
compatibility.inline_reload_note: A readable inline native reload may identify its actual about:srcdoc URL; GET-only HTTP(S) saver policy remains unchanged. This is request metadata, not a new public API or network-success guarantee.
